<reason>B identified and exploited the debate's decisive concession: A's opening admitted "forever was never literal" and defended reuse-after-long-rest, which B converted into the spine of every later speech — permanence is already dead under CON's own scheme, so the only question is whether the city ends the promise honestly or bills the future at hectares of cost. B answered both pressure questions with concrete institutions (memorial groves, columbaria, treatment plants) and its closing turned A's own "entire moral work of a grave" line into the kill shot. A fought hard and won the religious-affordability sub-clash — B never fully squared how a poor family whose faith forbids both composting and grave-disturbance gets served, and A's exemption carve-out went unanswered — but A never re-engaged the land arithmetic after conceding permanence, leaving its values defense resting on a delay B had already priced. B's clipped Rebuttal 1 is a real execution cost and keeps this short of a solid-win margin.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 1 reframed A's "reuse after long rest" as a confession that permanence is finished ("a lottery with a time bomb"), then B's closing quoted A4.1's "decades... are the entire moral work of a grave" and answered: "decades end. The grave is reclaimed, the promise broken, the hectares spent." A never escaped that frame, and its honest answer (the delay IS the moral work) only fed it.</best_rebuttal>
